source.title: Wan: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models
source.authors: Team Wan; Ang Wang; Baole Ai; Bin Wen; Chaojie Mao; Chen-Wei Xie; Di Chen; Feiwu Yu; Haiming Zhao; Jianxiao Yang; Jianyuan Zeng; Jiayu Wang; Jingfeng Zhang; Jingren Zhou; Jinkai Wang; Jixuan Chen; Kai Zhu; Kang Zhao; Keyu Yan; Lianghua Huang; Mengyang Feng; Ningyi Zhang; Pandeng Li; Pingyu Wu; Ruihang Chu; Ruili Feng; Shiwei Zhang; Siyang Sun; Tao Fang; Tianxing Wang; Tianyi Gui; Tingyu Weng; Tong Shen; Wei Lin; Wei Wang; Wei Wang; Wenmeng Zhou; Wente Wang; Wenting Shen; Wenyuan Yu; Xianzhong Shi; Xiaoming Huang; Xin Xu; Yan Kou; Yangyu Lv; Yifei Li; Yijing Liu; Yiming Wang; Yingya Zhang; Yitong Huang; Yong Li; You Wu; Yu Liu; Yulin Pan; Yun Zheng; Yuntao Hong; Yupeng Shi; Yutong Feng; Zeyinzi Jiang; Zhen Han; Zhi-Fan Wu; Ziyu Liu

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares training loss across architecture configurations in a text-to-image diffusion model, a different setting and measure from the language-model scaling-law claim.
record.gate_note: The paper says Wan demonstrates video-generation scaling with data and model size, and compares 1.3B and 14B models on generation benchmarks. It does not fit or report a power law in held-out loss, tokens, or compute; those benchmark scores therefore do not test the power-law versions. The AdaLN ablation reports training-loss curves and text descriptions, but no numeric loss values. Other reported evaluations and ablations do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is a technical report on the Wan video diffusion models. The abstract says the 14B model demonstrates scaling laws with data and model size, but the paper fits no power law and reports no loss against parameters, tokens or compute. The 1.3B vs 14B comparison uses only generation-benchmark scores. The AdaLN ablation compares four text-to-image diffusion configurations by training loss, shown only as curves. That is a design ablation on a different kind of system, not language-model pretraining loss. None of these results bears on any version as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is mostly right. In the ablation, the authors conclude that spending parameters on depth beats spending them on AdaLN, so they adopt fully shared AdaLN to cut parameters while preserving performance. Separately, the abstract asserts that the 14B model demonstrates video scaling laws in data and model size. That assertion is backed only by benchmark comparisons with the 1.3B model and other systems, not by any fitted law.
record.recipe_differences: This is a video and image diffusion-model report, not a language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling study. The relevant ablation compares training losses across AdaLN architectures; it does not fit scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The AdaLN sharing and depth configuration changes the reported training-loss ordering; the fully shared 1.5B configuration is described as consistently lowest.

fits_no_version.finding: Wan 14B outscores Wan 1.3B on Wan-Bench (0.724 vs 0.689; Table 2) and on VBench total score (86.22% vs 83.96%; Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within one video diffusion family, the larger model scores higher on video-generation benchmarks. This is a two-point size comparison with no fitted scaling relation.

fits_no_version.finding: In text-to-image diffusion ablations at 200k steps, the deeper fully shared AdaLN 1.5B model reaches the lowest training loss. The 1.7B non-shared model does not beat it, and the 1.3B model is slightly higher. The evidence is curves only (Fig. 16).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In DiT diffusion models, putting parameters into depth rather than per-block AdaLN lowers training loss more.

record.problems: The relevant AdaLN ablation reports training-loss curves without numeric values or uncertainty estimates. It evaluates text-to-image training loss, not held-out loss, and does not establish the magnitude or generality of the architecture effects.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were omitted. Other benchmark and ablation results measure video or image generation quality, VAE reconstruction, or unrelated components rather than the versions tested here.

untested.parts: No loss vs parameters, tokens or compute is reported.
No fitted law and no extrapolation.
No language-model loss across shapes at fixed size. The only shape comparison is one diffusion pair with no numbers.
Video and image models are studied, but no power-law form in loss is fit or shown. The scaling claim rests on benchmark scores of two model sizes.
Only two model sizes are compared on benchmarks, with no predictive relation to scale or loss.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2/tests classification and the V4 limits_scope label are dropped. The AdaLN ablation is on an image diffusion model, the loss is unquantified, and the parameter counts differ across configurations, so it does not measure V4's language-model loss claim. The 'scaling laws' wording in the abstract is an unsupported assertion.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
The ablation measures training loss for text-to-image models, not held-out language-model loss, and does not test a wide range of architectures.
The paper reports video-generation benchmark comparisons, but does not test whether a power-law form holds in video or other modalities or regimes.
Predictability of downstream-task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.

rows.subject: Full-shared-adaLN-1.3B
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch for text-to-image task; 200,000 steps
rows.operation_detail: Trained with fully shared AdaLN across all 30 attention blocks.
rows.measure: L2 loss between generated images and real images in latent space during training
rows.note: The text says this model, despite having fewer parameters, has slightly higher training loss than the other configurations; numeric values are not reported.
rows.check: Text-to-image diffusion training loss (flow-matching MSE, shown only in a figure). This is not language-model held-out loss, so it does not measure V4's system. It is also an architecture-design ablation across different parameter counts, not a fixed-size shape sweep.

rows.subject: Half-shared-adaLN-1.5B
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch for text-to-image task; 200,000 steps
rows.operation_detail: Shared AdaLN in the first 15 attention blocks and not shared in the remaining blocks.

conditions.value: AdaLN shared in first 15 blocks only

rows.measure: L2 loss between generated images and real images in latent space during training
rows.note: Compared with the same-size fully shared configuration, the text says this configuration does not achieve the lowest training loss; the magnitude is not stated.
rows.check: Same issue as r1: diffusion training loss, figure only, with no magnitude stated. It does not bear on V4 as named.

rows.subject: Full-shared-AdaLN-1.5B (extended)
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch for text-to-image task; 200,000 steps
rows.operation_detail: Shared AdaLN across all attention blocks; depth increased to 35 layers.
rows.measure: L2 loss between generated images and real images in latent space during training
rows.note: The text says this model consistently achieves the lowest training loss compared with the half-shared 1.5B model. The size of the difference is not stated.
rows.check: Same issue as r1. The depth-35 vs half-shared comparison at 1.5B is a shape comparison, but in an image diffusion model, with no numeric loss and a single pair.

rows.subject: Non-shared-AdaLN-1.7B

rows.operation_detail: AdaLN not shared across blocks; depth remains at 30 layers.
rows.measure: L2 loss between generated images and real images in latent space during training
rows.note: The text says this higher-parameter model does not outperform the fully shared 1.5B model; the magnitude is not stated.
rows.check: Same issue as r1: diffusion training loss, figure only.
